text:
Recent research supports separating product relationships from user relevance. The 2024 [complementary recommendation survey](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16135) highlights asymmetric complementarity and coexistence of substitution and complementarity; similarity alone cannot establish which relationship applies. [Counterfactual Implicit Feedback Modeling (NeurIPS 2025)](https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2025/hash/1436e87a58b3e6ac177450bd10721726-Abstract-Conference.html) treats implicit feedback as positive-unlabeled and affected by exposure bias. Missing interactions therefore do not establish dislike. The October 2026 preprint [Evidence Before Sampling](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.07708) likewise frames negative-candidate discovery around behavioral evidence rather than absence alone.

A practical adaptation is an auditable, abstaining rule system. [Snorkel’s foundational work](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7075849/) provides labeling functions that vote or abstain, then combine noisy, correlated signals into probabilistic labels; regex and heuristic functions require no pretrained weights. Proposed audit labels: supported complement when explicit accessory/fit language links identifiable products; possible substitute when function and specifications overlap; specification conflict only when explicit requirements contradict candidate specifications; insufficient evidence otherwise. Preserve the exact title/description spans and historical events behind each judgment. Temporal co-occurrence can provide weak support, but cannot establish compatibility, continued ownership, satisfaction, or causal complementarity. Report rule coverage, abstention, conflicting votes, and missing specifications separately; these are evidence diagnostics, not relevance ground truth. This four-way audit is a synthesis of the sources, not an established benchmark taxonomy.
